column3: MT 6:2. “Who will be over” is rendered “that they should be in charge of.”
MT 6:3. “Overseers” is rendered “commissioners”; NASB adds parentheses, and renders “giving report” as “accountable” and “suffering injury” as “suffer loss.”
MT 6:4. “A spirit extraordinary was in him” is rendered “he possessed an extraordinary spirit”; NASB adds “began.”
MT 6:5. “Occasion” is rendered “ground of accusation,” “from the side of the kingdom” “in regard to government affairs,” and “trustworthy” “faithful”; NASB adds “evidence of.”
MT 6:6. Close to the Aramaic.
MT 6:7. “Came as a crowd” is rendered “came by agreement”; the meaning of the Aramaic verb is uncertain.
MT 6:8. “Make stringent a prohibition” is rendered “enforce an injunction,” and “counselors” “high officials.”
MT 6:9. “Writing” is rendered “document,” and “pass away” “be revoked.”
MT 6:10. NASB adds “that is.”
MT 6:11. NASB puts the window clause in parentheses with “now,” adds “continued,” and renders “praising” as “giving thanks.”
MT 6:12. “Came as a crowd” is rendered “came by agreement,” and “imploring favor” “supplication.”
MT 6:13. “The word is certain” is rendered “The statement is true.”
MT 6:14. “Has not set discretion to you” is rendered “pays no attention to you”; NASB adds “but keeps.”
MT 6:15. “It was exceedingly displeasing to him” is rendered “he was deeply distressed,” and “the goings in of the sun” “sunset.”
MT 6:16. Close to the Aramaic.
MT 6:17. The active “they brought … they threw” is rendered as passives; “in continuance” is rendered “constantly.”
MT 6:18. NASB adds “own.”
MT 6:19. The Aramaic word rendered “entertainment” is uncertain.
MT 6:20. Close to the Aramaic.
MT 6:21. “Pained” is rendered “troubled”; “in continuance” is rendered “constantly.”
MT 6:22. Close to the Aramaic.
MT 6:23. “Innocence was found to me” is rendered “I was found innocent,” and “a hurtful act” “crime.”
MT 6:24. “It was exceedingly good to him” is rendered “the king was very pleased”; NASB adds “whatever.”
MT 6:25. “Had eaten his pieces” (an idiom) is rendered “had maliciously accused”; “sons” is rendered “children,” and “assaulted” “overpowered.”
MT 6:26. “Languages” is rendered “men of every language,” and “earth” “land.”
MT 6:27. NASB supplies “men are to”; “to the end” is rendered “forever.”
MT 6:28. “Hand” is rendered “power”; NASB adds “also.”
MT 6:29. “Prospered” is rendered “enjoyed success.”
